questions.question: Explain fairness as a journalistic principle
questions.solution_html:
• Explain fairness as a journalistic principle U] / [CO1]
  • Fairness requires journalists to explore and present all sides of a story. This means giving equal
  • opportunity for different perspectives to be heard, especially in contentious or complex issues.
  • Journalists should prioritize truth and transparency over speed or popularity, ensuring the public
  • receives trustworthy content.

questions.question: Analyse why fact-checking is crucial in the digital news environment.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse why fact-checking is crucial in the digital news environment- / [CO4]
  • Fact-checking helps prevent the viral spread of falsehoods that can mislead the public. In a fast-paced
  • digital environment, maintaining trust is essential. Fact-checking ensures that journalists uphold
  • integrity and accuracy, reinforcing public confidence in their reporting. Digital journalism benefits
  • from tools like reverse image searches, geolocation, and AI-assisted verification. These technologies
  • enhance the ability to detect and correct misinformation efficiently.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is indepth journalism
questions.solution_html:
• What is in-depth journalism / [CO1]
  • In-depth journalism involves extensive research and reporting to uncover the full scope of a story.
  • Journalists dig deep into facts, data, and sources to provide a comprehensive understanding of
  • complex issues. It goes beyond surface-level reporting by offering background, context, and expert
  • analysis. This helps readers grasp the significance and implications of the story.

questions.question: Elaborate the idea of citizen media and its growing salience in the present
questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate the idea of citizen media and its growing salience in the present / [CO1]
  • Citizen media allows everyday people—not just professional journalists—to report news, share
  • opinions, and document events using smartphones, blogs, and social platforms. This democratizes
  • information and gives voice to underrepresented communities. Real-Time, On-the-Ground Reporting,
  • It amplifies Marginalized Voices and fuelled by Technology and social media. As citizen media grows,
  • mainstream outlets are adapting by incorporating user-generated content and engaging with
  • grassroots narratives. It’s reshaping how news is sourced, verified, and consumed

questions.question: In the world of media, images can make or break a news. Discuss
questions.solution_html:
• In the world of media, images can make or break a news. Discuss / [CO1]
  • Images evoke emotions faster than words. A powerful photo can stir empathy, outrage, or hope,
  • making the story more compelling and memorable. It enhances comprehension, authenticates the
  • story. Manipulated images can distort facts, sensationalize events, or reinforce bias. Ethical image
  • selection is crucial to maintain journalistic integrity. In the age of social media, striking visuals are
  • more likely to be clicked, shared, and remembered. They often determine whether a story goes viral
  • or gets ignored.

questions.question: Recall the challenges faced by citizen journalists while reporting.
questions.solution_html:
• Challenges Faced by Citizen Journalists:
  • o Lack of Legal & Physical Protection: Susceptibility to harassment, arrest, violence,
  • and legal threats without institutional backing.
  • o Ethical & Credibility Deficits: Risk of spreading unverified information, lacking formal
  • training in verification, defamation laws, or journalistic standards.
  • o Resource Constraints: Limited funding, professional camera/audio equipment, and
  • editing infrastructure.
  • o Algorithmic Shadowbanning & Censorship: Account suspensions, platform policy
  • changes, internet blackouts, and government censorship.
questions.source_exam: III Semester MGU-UGP-(Hons) 2024 Admission Regular(Special Examination) Examination July 2026

questions.question: Explain the significance of journalistic ethics in today's information ecosystem.
questions.solution_html:
• Significance of Journalistic Ethics:
  • o Combating Disinformation: Essential for filtering out deepfakes, paid news, and
  • sensationalized misinformation in digital spaces.
  • o Preserving Public Trust: Upholding accuracy, objectivity, and fairness maintains
  • democratic reliance on news.
  • o Harm Minimization: Respecting privacy, protecting vulnerable sources/minors, and
  • preventing hate speech or panic.
  • o Accountability: Ensuring rights of reply, corrections, and conflict-of-interest
  • disclosures.
questions.source_exam: III Semester MGU-UGP-(Hons) 2024 Admission Regular(Special Examination) Examination July 2026

questions.question: Trace the history and growth of citizen journalism.
questions.solution_html:
• History and Growth of Citizen Journalism:
  • o Early Roots: Pamphleteering, public forums, and early open-publishing networks
  • (e.g., Indymedia late 1990s).
  • o Milestone Events: Coverage of the 2004 Asian Tsunami, 2005 London Bombings, and
  • 2009 Iranian Protests using early camera phones and blogs.
  • o Social Media Boom: Arab Spring (2011) and widespread adoption of platforms like
  • Twitter/X, Facebook, YouTube, and WhatsApp.
  • o Modern Era: Integration of MoJo (Mobile Journalism) tools, livestreaming, hyper-
  • local blogging, and citizen-led watchdog networks.
questions.source_exam: III Semester MGU-UGP-(Hons) 2024 Admission Regular(Special Examination) Examination July 2026

questions.question: Recall the techniques used in interviews. [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Techniques Used in Interviews:
  • o Preparation & Research: Topic backgrounding, defining goals, and drafting open-
  • ended key questions.
  • o Questioning Strategies: Moving from general warm-up queries to specific probing
  • questions; using follow-ups based on active listening.
  • o Building Rapport: Establishing trust, active body language, maintaining neutral non-
  • verbal cues, and handling sensitive topics with empathy.
  • o Technical Execution: Recording permissions, microphone positioning, ambient noise
  • control, and clear note-taking/transcription discipline.
questions.source_exam: III Semester MGU-UGP-(Hons) 2024 Admission Regular(Special Examination) Examination July 2026
